R001.fact: For a C¹ curve v:I→R^m on an open real interval, (v·v)'=2v·v'. In the Euclidean norm v·v=|v|²; hence |v|=1 throughout I implies v·v'=0 throughout I.

R001.fact: For a C² curve v:I→R^m on an open interval, (v·v)''=2|v'|²+2v·v''. For a smooth map on R^n×(0,∞), this applies along time and each spatial coordinate line, with v',v'' equal to the corresponding classical partial derivatives. If the map has unit norm, u·u_tt=−|u_t|² and u·∂_{x_jx_j}u=−|∂_{x_j}u|² at every point and every spatial index j.

R001.justification: For each component differentiate v_k² twice: (v_k²)''=2(v'_k)²+2v_k v''_k. Sum over finitely many components. C is compact.

R002.justification: Compact sets in Hausdorff Euclidean space are closed: separating a point outside the compact set from its points and taking a finite subcover gives an exterior neighborhood.
